stem: A client requires Droplet Precautions. Which action should the nurse take when entering the client's room or patient space?

options.A: Enter without facial PPE unless an aerosol-generating procedure is planned
options.B: Use a fit-tested N95 respirator for routine droplet care because a medical mask is inadequate
options.C: Require a negative-pressure airborne infection isolation room for all droplet infections
options.D: Don a mask upon entry into the patient room or patient space

rationale: CDC Transmission-Based Precautions guidance states that healthcare personnel should use PPE appropriately for Droplet Precautions and don a mask upon entry into the patient room or patient space. Routine Droplet Precautions do not require special air handling or a negative-pressure room. D is correct.
educational_objective: Apply the core PPE requirement for Droplet Precautions at room entry.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Droplet Precautions section — use PPE appropriately; don mask upon entry into patient room or patient space
source_claim_supported: For Droplet Precautions, healthcare personnel don a mask upon entry; special air handling/ventilation is not required for routine droplet transmission.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Droplet Precautions

source_original.stem: A client is placed on droplet precautions. The nurse should ensure that:

options.A: Signage placed only inside the room, not at the entrance
options.B: Signage only needed for airborne, not droplet, precautions
options.C: No signage needed, since staff should already know the type
options.D: Clear signage posted at the entrance before any entry

source_original.rationale: Clear signage indicating the specific type of isolation precautions in place and the required PPE should be posted at the room entrance (visible before entry), ensuring all staff, visitors, and ancillary personnel are informed and can don appropriate PPE before entering, regardless of the specific precaution type (contact, droplet, or airborne).
source_original.source_detail: Transmission-based precautions: precaution signage/PPE instructions at point of entry under facility isolation protocol; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced a weakly sourced universal signage claim with CDC's direct Droplet Precautions requirement to don a mask upon room/patient-space entry. Kept the same blueprint category and correct-option letter while making the item clinically stronger and source-verifiable.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC Transmission-Based Precautions guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.claim_audit: Mask upon entry and lack of routine special air handling are directly supported by CDC.

distractor_audit.A: Routine entry still requires the droplet mask indicated by CDC.
distractor_audit.B: A fit-tested N95 is not the routine Droplet Precautions requirement.
distractor_audit.C: Droplet transmission does not itself mandate an AIIR.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: D is uniquely correct for routine droplet care as written.
audit_findings.cueing: Removed the signage-only distractor pattern and used clinically plausible isolation choices.
audit_findings.blueprint: Transmission-based precautions map directly to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC Droplet Precautions section; D remains uniquely correct.
